AL: Alabama is nicknamed the Yellowhammer State after the yellowhammer bird, a symbol linked to Alabama soldiers in the Civil War.
AK: Alaska is called the Last Frontier because of its vast wilderness, remote lands, and late development compared with most U.S. states.
AZ: Arizona is the Grand Canyon State because it is home to the Grand Canyon, one of the world’s most famous natural landmarks.
AR: Arkansas is called the Natural State to highlight its mountains, forests, rivers, and outdoor scenery.
CA: California is the Golden State, a name tied to the 1848 Gold Rush and the state’s sunny golden landscapes.
CO: Colorado is called the Centennial State because it joined the Union in 1876, 100 years after U.S. independence.
CT: Connecticut is the Constitution State because it is linked to the Fundamental Orders of 1639, seen as an early constitution.
DE: Delaware is called the First State because it was the first to ratify the U.S. Constitution in 1787.
FL: Florida is the Sunshine State because of its warm climate and abundant sunshine.
GA: Georgia is called the Peach State because peaches became one of its best-known crops.
HI: Hawaii is the Aloha State because aloha is a famous Hawaiian word for greeting, love, and kindness.
ID: Idaho is called the Gem State because it is rich in many gemstones and other natural resources.
IL: Illinois is the Prairie State because much of its land was once covered by open prairie grasslands.
IN: Indiana is called the Hoosier State because Hoosier became the long-standing nickname for people from Indiana.
IA: Iowa is the Hawkeye State, likely honoring Chief Black Hawk and the region’s early history.
KS: Kansas is called the Sunflower State because wild sunflowers grow widely across the state.
KY: Kentucky is the Bluegrass State because its limestone-rich soil helps produce bluegrass pastures.
LA: Louisiana is called the Pelican State because the brown pelican is a historic state symbol.
ME: Maine is the Pine Tree State because of its many pine forests and timber history.
MD: Maryland is called the Old Line State in honor of the Maryland Line troops of the Revolutionary War.
MA: Massachusetts is the Bay State because several large bays shape its coastline.
MI: Michigan is called the Wolverine State, though the exact origin is uncertain and may date to early frontier times.
MN: Minnesota is the Land of 10,000 Lakes because it has thousands of lakes across the state.
MS: Mississippi is called the Magnolia State because magnolia trees and flowers are strongly associated with it.
MO: Missouri is the Show Me State, a nickname linked to a tradition of practical skepticism and wanting proof.
MT: Montana is called Big Sky Country because of its wide-open plains and huge, dramatic skies.
NE: Nebraska is the Cornhusker State because corn farming has long been central to its agriculture.
NV: Nevada is called the Silver State because silver mining played a major role in its history and economy.
NH: New Hampshire is the Granite State because of its abundant granite formations and quarries.
NJ: New Jersey is called the Garden State because of its long history of fertile farms and market gardening.
NM: New Mexico is the Land of Enchantment because of its striking scenery and distinctive cultural heritage.
NY: New York is called the Empire State because of its historic wealth, power, and influence.
NC: North Carolina is the Tar Heel State, a name linked to its historic tar, pitch, and turpentine industry.
ND: North Dakota is called the Peace Garden State after the International Peace Garden on the U.S.-Canada border.
OH: Ohio is the Buckeye State because buckeye trees are closely associated with the state.
OK: Oklahoma is called the Sooner State after settlers known as Sooners who entered the territory early.
OR: Oregon is the Beaver State because beavers were important in the region’s fur-trade era.
PA: Pennsylvania is the Keystone State because of its central role among the original 13 colonies and in U.S. founding.
RI: Rhode Island is called the Ocean State because it has extensive shoreline relative to its small size.
SC: South Carolina is the Palmetto State because the palmetto tree became a major state symbol.
SD: South Dakota is called the Mount Rushmore State because Mount Rushmore is one of its best-known landmarks.
TN: Tennessee is the Volunteer State because many Tennesseans volunteered for military service, especially in 1812.
TX: Texas is called the Lone Star State because the single star on its flag symbolizes independent spirit.
UT: Utah is the Beehive State because the beehive symbolizes industry, thrift, and hard work.
VT: Vermont is the Green Mountain State because its name comes from the French words for green mountains.
VA: Virginia is called the Mother of Presidents because eight U.S. presidents were born there.
WA: Washington is the Evergreen State because its forests stay green through much of the year.
WV: West Virginia is called the Mountain State because it lies almost entirely within the Appalachian Mountains.
WI: Wisconsin is the Badger State because early lead miners often lived in hillside shelters like badger burrows.
WY: Wyoming is called the Equality State because it led the nation in granting women voting rights.
